kaps_punt: Weeklikse lees deur leerders: lees vir genot: Lees oor religiee in Suid-Afrika.

items.bewering: Vrydagmiddag klink daar 'n stem oor die dakke van die huise. Dit is die oproep tot gebed by die moskee om die hoek.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Friday prayer' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friday_prayer): Jumu'ah is held at midday every Friday, replacing the Zuhr prayer, and 'a muezzin will recite a specific chant called an adhan to call the congregation to the mosque', usually 15-20 minutes before it. Wikipedia, 'Muezzin' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muezzin): the call is given by a human voice, today often through loudspeakers on the minaret. South African practice of an audible adhan: IOL 2020-09-18 'Loudspeakers in mosques debate' and Cape Times 2018-12-07 'Adhan volume concerns' (Cape Town mosques). Kanttekening by die stel-toets: die adhan word vyf keer per dag geroep, nie net op Vrydae nie. Die teks se nie dat dit net Vrydag gebeur nie, en die sin 'Op Vrydae kom meer mense daar bymekaar as op ander dae' hou die ander dae oop, dus is die stuk nie vals nie.

items.bewering: Die minaret staan hoër as die bome aan daardie kant van die straat.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Muezzin' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muezzin): historically the call was recited from the top of the minaret so that it carried to people nearby, and loudspeakers are now mounted on top of it. A minaret is a mosque's tower. The comparison with these particular trees is part of the story and can't be checked, but it fits what a minaret is.

items.bewering: Yusuf en sy pa trek netjiese klere aan en stap moskee toe.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Friday prayer': attendance is 'strictly incumbent upon all adult males', and women and children are not under the same obligation. On clothing: islamonline.net, 'Jumu'ah: Friday congregational prayer', and riwaya.co.uk, 'How to pray Jummah prayer'. Both say that on Friday it is Sunnah to bathe and to put on clean, good clothes before going to the mosque.

items.bewering: Op Vrydae kom meer mense daar bymekaar as op ander dae.
items.bron: Britannica, 'jumʿah' (https://www.britannica.com/topic/jumah), as given in the search summary because the page itself returned 403: the Friday noon service is one that adult male Muslims are obliged to attend, ideally in one central mosque per locality, with a sizeable gathering. Wikipedia, 'Friday prayer': it is obligatory for men. The daily prayers carry no such obligation to attend the mosque. No survey that measures Friday against weekday attendance was found. The comparison follows directly from the obligation, and it is the reason the Friday congregation is the large one. The sentence is a comparative and so is recorded here as a superlative.

items.bewering: In die maand Ramadan eet sy gesin in die donker voor dagbreek. Daarna eet hulle eers weer wanneer die son gesak het.
items.bron: Islamic Relief Canada, 'What is iftar and suhoor?' (https://www.islamicreliefcanada.org/resources/what-is-iftar-and-suhoor), and Review of Religions, 'Suhoor & Iftar: when do Muslims begin and break the fast during Ramadan' (https://www.reviewofreligions.org/30478/). Suhoor is the meal eaten before dawn and before the Fajr adhan. The fast is broken at iftar, at sunset, at the time of the Maghrib prayer.

items.bewering: Vrydag net voor sononder ... Binne staan twee kerse op die tafel waar die gesin gaan eet. Sara se ma steek hulle aan
items.bron: Chabad.org, 'What Are Shabbat Candles' (https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/93783): the basic custom is two candles, lit by the woman of the house, 'often in the dining room where the festive holiday meal will soon take place'. Chabad.org, 'The time for lighting' and Jewish Press, 'The time for lighting candles': they are lit about 18 minutes before sunset, and at the latest just before it. The story's later sentence, that Thandi rides home while it is still light, agrees with this.

items.bewering: en hulle brand die hele aand deur.
items.bron: Chabad.org, 'What Are Shabbat Candles', staff comment: 'On Shabbat we may not extinguish flames, the candles are left to burn out on their own'. Most Shabbat candles burn for about three hours. Chabad.org, 'How Long Should Shabbat Candles Burn' (aid/7144147): ideally they burn as long as people are up in the house, and at least through the Friday-night meal. My Jewish Learning, 'Lighting Shabbat Candles': they are not put out but allowed to burn all the way down. 'Die hele aand deur' is a fair picture of candles that are lit just before sunset and burn for about three hours.

items.bewering: Saterdagoggend stap Sara en haar ouma in hulle beste klere by Thandi verby.
items.bron: NJOP, 'Shabbat clothes' (https://njop.org/shabbat-clothes/). Jewish Press, Rabbi Pruzansky and Rabbi Enkin on Shabbat clothing. Oz Torah, 'A change of clothes'. All three cite the Talmud, Maimonides and the Shulchan Aruch: honouring Shabbat includes wearing clean, special clothing that is better than weekday clothing, and the Shulchan Aruch compares it to dressing for a formal occasion. The superlative 'beste klere' is supported.

items.bewering: Hulle loop elke Saterdag die drie blokke na die sinagoge toe.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Driving on Shabbat' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driving_on_Shabbat): Orthodox law forbids driving on Shabbat except to save a life, and Orthodox Jews live within walking distance of a synagogue so that they can walk. Synagogue visitor guides say the same: shaarei.org and bhhc-shul.org. The service is on Saturday morning. This is one family's practice, which matches observant practice, and the story does not claim that every Jew does it.

items.bewering: Die familie kom vandag bymekaar vir 'n besondere geleentheid wat nie elke week gebeur nie. ... Sy steek impepho aan
items.bron: Zondi, N. & Ntshangase, M. (2013), 'Shifting Boundaries in Respect of Perceptions Governing Women and the Burning of Impepho', Alternation 20(2): 218-235, UKZN (https://alternation.ukzn.ac.za/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/12-Zon-min.pdf). It describes impepho as an indigenous plant that is dried and 'burnt in order to communicate with one's ancestors', used at particular ceremonies and feasts: umemulo, isifo (death), ukubuyisa, and occasions of thanksgiving. These are occasions, not a weekly gathering. International Society for Ethnopharmacology, 'Helichrysum; a ritual plant' (photo essay), and Wikipedia, 'Helichrysum petiolare', support impepho as a Helichrysum burnt to communicate with the ancestors. Contrast in the set: the story correctly does not present this as a weekly day like Friday, Saturday or Sunday.

items.bewering: Ouma Nomsa ... Sy steek impepho aan (by 'n byeenkoms van die uitgebreide familie by Thandi se huis)
items.bron: The sources disagree on who lights impepho at a family ceremony, and the story makes a specific choice. Zondi & Ntshangase (2013, Alternation 20(2), UKZN), abstract: 'Males, albeit of particular standing within the family are charged with presiding powers at such ceremonies. Ordinarily, women have no place in these matters.' The same article reports that women over fifty who head their own households do burn it and preside, sometimes privately, and that this is a growing but contested shift. A UBC Museum of Anthropology page on impepho (blogs.ubc.ca/amaguguethu) says the person who burns it is 'the elderly, the head of the family, or a specific person tasked with that duty' and that 'women cannot be that person'. An older ethnographic note (KCAL, James Stuart Archive vol. 4, 1986, Msimanga) does describe an old woman, perhaps the grandmother, burning impepho in her hut. So it is not false that a grandmother lights impepho. The documented norm, however, is that at a gathering of the wider family for an occasion, held at her child's house, the presiding elder is usually a man. A learner may read this as the typical picture of the practice. Customs differ between groups and families, and the story does not name a group. This is a question about how a living practice is portrayed, and a writer cannot settle it from sources. A person should decide whether to keep it as it is (attested and growing), or to describe the act without tying it to a specific family role.

items.bewering: 'n dun wit rook trek stadig oor die muur.
items.bron: NCJRS abstract no. 72891 (US National Criminal Justice Reference Service) on smoke colour: white or light grey smoke is usually associated with paper, straw, leaves or wood, and forms from condensed pyrolysis products. Impepho is a dried plant bundle that smoulders: International Society for Ethnopharmacology, 'Helichrysum; a ritual plant' and Zondi & Ntshangase 2013. No source describes impepho smoke specifically, but white-grey smoke is what dry, smouldering plant material produces. 'Dun' is a description of a small amount lit outdoors, not a factual claim.

items.bewering: Sondagoggend lui die klok van die kerk bo in die straat.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Church bell' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_bell): the main function is to call worshippers to a communal service. WELS, 'Church bells' (https://wels.net/faq/church-bells/), and Westbury Parish Church, 'Bells and Bellringers': bells are rung before the Sunday services. Sunday as Christianity's main day of worship is consistent across these sources. Not every church has a bell, but the story is about one church.

items.bewering: Thandi hoor van die pad af hoe die mense binne die kerk sing.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Hymn of the day' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hymn_of_the_day). Dialogue Journal vol. 50 no. 3, 'From the pulpit: the song of the righteous...'. UUA, 'Liturgy for Hymn Sing Sunday'. All three describe congregational singing as a standard part of Christian Sunday services across denominations.

items.bewering: Later in die jaar brand daar klein lampies op die Naidoos se voormuur. Dit is Divali, die fees van die ligte
items.bron: Royal Ontario Museum, 'Good Over Evil: Diwali, Festival of Lights' (https://www.rom.on.ca/blogs/good-over-evil-diwali-festival-lights). McGill MORSL, Diwali. Michigan State University Provost, Diwali fact sheet. Together they establish Diwali as the festival of lights, with diyas (small clay oil lamps) set out in rows in windows, at doorways and outside the house. IOL / The Post, 2025-10-19, 'Diwali lights up South Africa with joy and reflection': in South Africa, lamps are placed at entrances, and Hindu communities in Chatsworth, Phoenix, Lenasia and Rylands celebrate it. Wikipedia, 'Kartika (month)': Diwali falls on the new moon of Kartika, mid-October to mid-November, so 'later in die jaar' is a once-a-year festival and the story does not present it as a weekly day. 'Klein vlammetjies' agrees with oil lamps. The surname Naidoo is South African Indian; the story does not claim the family's religion, so there is no claim to check there.

items.bewering: Sy ma steek intussen die laaste lampies langs die hek aan.
items.bron: IOL / The Post 2025-10-19 (lamps at entrances, to invite blessings) and the Royal Ontario Museum (diyas at doorways and outside buildings): lamps at the gate and entrance fit the documented practice.

items.bewering: Sy hoef nie na 'n kalender te kyk om te weet watter dag dit is nie. Die mense in die straat wys dit vir haar. (die straat as kalender, gelees saam met die hele week se gelowe)
items.bron: Mapping tested on the set of faiths together. Friday is the Muslim day of congregational prayer: Wikipedia and Britannica, 'Friday prayer / jumʿah'. Shabbat begins at sunset on Friday, with candles, and the synagogue service is on Saturday: Chabad.org and Wikipedia, 'Driving on Shabbat'. Sunday is the Christian day of worship: Wikipedia, 'Church bell'. The story keeps the contrasts right. The ancestral gathering is explicitly 'nie elke week nie' (Zondi & Ntshangase 2013), and Divali is 'later in die jaar', once a year (Wikipedia, 'Kartika'). Neither is wrongly presented as a weekly day marker, and none of the stated contrasts is false. Limit of the comparison: the street marks only Friday to Sunday, not Monday to Thursday. A learner may take it that only these three days can be 'seen', but that is not a false claim about a religion. The story does not suggest that Islam's Friday is a day of rest, and does not suggest that the adhan is heard only on Fridays (see the first item).

opsomming: Everything about the faiths checks out, and read as a set their contrasts are true, but a person must decide whether a grandmother should light impepho at the family gathering, because UKZN research (Zondi & Ntshangase 2013) says men of standing usually preside at such ceremonies, while women who head households increasingly do it too.
